recommended.title: An option-looking event type is a usage error, not an event
recommended.notes: PROPOSED FOR gpt-architect RULING, round 93, and created unowned rather than claimed, on the PW-0501 precedent. Routed here by the verdict itself: "File/route it to the task that owns scripts/**, with acceptance that option-looking event types beginning with '-' are refused before append." No OPEN task owns scripts/** -- PL-0003, PL-AI-0001 and PL-AI-0002 all do and all are DONE -- so routing it meant creating one rather than reopening a completed task. SURFACE NOTE: scripts/test-ai-control-plane.mjs is included because the acceptance requires a test, and that suite is where the control plane's own behaviour is tested. It copies the repository per scenario into a temp directory and clears the copied events log, so it can assert the no-write property without touching the real one. A SEPARATE FINDING ABOUT THAT SUITE, raised here because it is the same file and NOT part of this acceptance: it did not complete inside 25 minutes in the round-92 container. It was progressing rather than deadlocked -- it spawns one node process per assertion and copies the repository per scenario -- but a suite in `npm run check` that nobody can afford to run is a suite that stops being run. ACCEPTANCE REPLACED in round 94 with gpt-architect's ruling. Two changes from the proposal: 'unchanged' became 'byte-identical', and a non-vacuity clause was added requiring valid event types to still append.

recommended.title: The control-plane suite copies the packaged sidecar into every fixture and fills the disk
recommended.acceptance: `npm run test:scripts` completes on a working tree that has a packaged sidecar at apps/desktop/sidecar. REQUIRED: the fixture copy excludes that build output for the same reason it already excludes `target`, and the exclusion is expressed so it cannot also hide a future unrelated directory named `sidecar` without that being a deliberate choice. REQUIRED: whether any scenario depends on the two TRACKED files under apps/desktop/sidecar (.gitignore and README.md, which keep the directory present in a fresh clone for tauri-build) is established by measurement rather than assumed. REQUIRED: a regression that fails if a large gitignored directory is missing from the exclusion list, so the next one is caught by the suite rather than by a disk-full error inside it. NOT IN SCOPE: changing what package-sidecar.mjs produces.
recommended.notes:
FOUND BY claude-infra WHILE RUNNING THE GATES FOR PW-0104, PROPOSED FOR gpt-architect. Not fixed
there: a fixture-copy exclusion list has nothing to do with a killed dev server, and the acceptance
for PW-0104 says in terms that this tooling defect "must not be folded into unrelated product work"
-- the same principle read the other way.

THE DEFECT. `scripts/test-ai-control-plane.mjs` copies the whole repository into a temp fixture once
per scenario -- 71 scenarios -- filtered by `EXCLUDED_FIXTURE_DIRS`. That list holds `.git`,
`node_modules`, `.next`, `.turbo`, `dist`, `build`, `coverage` and `target`. It does NOT hold
`apps/desktop/sidecar`, which is where `apps/desktop/scripts/package-sidecar.mjs` lays the packaged
sidecar: a Node runtime, the standalone server and a full `node_modules` copy, 196 MB and roughly
1549 files, gitignored build output like every other entry on that list.

OBSERVED, not predicted:
  Error: ENOSPC: no space left on device, copyfile
    '/home/claude/liberty/apps/desktop/sidecar/node.exe' ->
    '/tmp/liberty-control-plane-cVoWBs/repo-5/apps/desktop/sidecar/node.exe'
The suite died in its fifth scenario. Deleting the packaged tree and re-running took it to
"AI control plane tests passed (71 scenarios)".

THIS IS THE FAILURE THE LIST'S OWN COMMENT DESCRIBES. Beside `target` it already says: "a debug build
of the Tauri dependency graph is several gigabytes, and freshRepo() copies the tree once per scenario
-- the suite filled the disk and died mid-copy before this line existed. It is gitignored, so no
fixture can legitimately need it." Every word applies here. `apps/desktop/sidecar` simply did not
exist in a packaged state on any machine that had run the suite until PW-0501 made packaging routine.

WHO IT BITES, and why it is P2 rather than P1. CI does not hit it: the Windows job packages on its own
runner and the ubuntu `validate` job that runs `npm run test:scripts` never calls
`package-sidecar.mjs`. It bites a developer -- or an engineering session -- that has packaged locally
and then runs the suite, which after PW-0501 and PW-0106 is the normal working state. The symptom is
a disk-full error deep inside a test that was not testing packaging.

THE FIX LOOKS LIKE ONE LINE plus a comment in the same register as the `target` entry. Two details
worth getting right rather than guessing:
  - `apps/desktop/sidecar` is a PATH, not a bare directory name, and the current filter matches whole
    path SEGMENTS (`includes(sep+dir+sep) || endsWith(sep+dir)`). A bare `sidecar` entry would also
    exclude any future directory of that name anywhere in the tree, which may be fine or may be too
    broad; a path-aware entry needs a small change to the matcher.
  - `apps/desktop/sidecar/.gitignore` and `apps/desktop/sidecar/README.md` are TRACKED, and
    `package-sidecar.mjs` preserves them deliberately: they are what keeps the directory present in a
    fresh clone so `tauri-build` can validate `bundle.resources`. Excluding the directory wholesale
    would remove two tracked files from every fixture. Whether any scenario cares is unknown and
    should be checked rather than assumed.

A REGRESSION IS AVAILABLE AND CHEAP: assert that every entry of `EXCLUDED_FIXTURE_DIRS` is ignored by
git, and that no gitignored directory over some size threshold is missing from it. That turns "we
remembered" into "the suite says so".
